transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

It is not faulty and you do not need to send it back. The AEG L7FEE865R's 'Eco 40-60' programme is designed to run for around 3 hours and 39 minutes to meet strict EU energy efficiency standards. It washes at lower temperatures for longer periods, which uses less electricity but takes much more time than older machines or quick wash cycles. However, we should confirm the machine is heating correctly in case there is an underlying issue. Please run a standard 60°C Cottons programme with a small load (like towels). When it finishes, check if the laundry is warm. If it is cold, that would indicate a heating fault; if it is warm, your machine is working perfectly.
I haven't run a 60 yet, so I can't say how that comes out. Is there anything else I can check on the Eco 40-60 itself, as that's the one I actually want to use?

There isn't really another check for the Eco 40-60 cycle itself other than seeing how it performs. The length is normal for this programme, but we need to be sure it's actually heating properly during those long hours. Please run one Eco 40-60 wash with a small load (like two towels). When it finishes:
1. Is the laundry warm or cold?
2. Did the machine spend most of that time tumbling, or did it seem to sit still in 'Wash' for a long time? If the clothes come out warm and it tumbled normally, your machine is working perfectly and you can use this cycle with confidence. If they are cold or it feels like it's stuck waiting, we'll need to look at the heating system.

I haven't done a small load, but on my full loads the door glass is only barely lukewarm. It spends long stretches just slowly tumbling, quietly, and the clothes do come out clean. Is that normal for this programme?

Yes, that is completely normal for the Eco 40-60 cycle. The machine saves energy by washing at a lower temperature for a longer time, which is why it takes nearly four hours and why the door glass stays only lukewarm (it never gets hot enough to be warm to the touch). Since your clothes are coming out clean on full loads, there is no evidence of a fault. You do not need to send it back. You can use this programme with confidence. If you ever want faster washing and don't mind using slightly more energy, you can switch to a 40°C or 60°C Cottons cycle instead.
